Carl — quick answers inline: 

A) Manual promotion: legacy runbook step was manual. Since July we push an automated promotion via orchestration ("auto-promote-on-restore" flag) for all production-serving pools. The runbook excerpt included the manual command (for emergency/manual intervention) but the automation covers standard failovers. Only SREs and on-call Leads are authorized to run manual promotion; the oncall_roster file indicates the Lead column. If you need the permissions matrix we can redact internal IDs and share.

B) 14:04:22Z spike: that correlates with a background telemetry aggregation job (index compaction) kicked on the node that also hosted the primary KV writer during the replay window. Because compaction is I/O heavy it pushed a few token-service requests into the slow tail for ~4-6s in rare samples. We have since adjusted compaction scheduling to avoid warm-failover windows. See short note in runbook_playback_notes_20270828.txt (line 48).

If that answers everything we can mark the BCP portion of the SIG as "closed (evidence attached)" on our end. Happy to join a short sync if Halcyon wants a walkthrough.

—Jordan Blake
Director, Customer Reliability, Redwood Inference
